_comment: How the loop reads a [verify] run that did or did not run to an exit (docs/CONTRACTS.md §1, #231).
Each case is the bash tool's result for the declared check; `outcome` is the record's `verify`, and
`handed_back` whether the turn is sent back to the model. `unrunnable` is what `gnomon check` calls
the same result (§6): the check never ran to an exit. Asserted by
packages/gnomon-core/src/verify_declined.test.ts, which runs the real loop against a scripted model

cases.name: declined by the person asked
cases.content: Refused: the user declined to run this command.

cases.name: timed out and killed
cases.content: Command timed out and was killed.

cases.name: refused by the sandbox
cases.content: Refused: [sandbox] exec = "os" is declared, and Windows has no OS sandbox.

cases.name: refused as a re-run after a timeout
cases.content: Refused: this command already timed out this turn.
cases.summary: bash — refused (already timed out this turn)
